I would like that part of the tape, that is to say, only that part when he was taken out of the car, and when he is told that he is under arrest, et cetera, to show that part of the tape to the expert witness before she presents her findings. And that is why it has to be a closed session, because that is an exhibit that the Prosecution asked not to be shown to the public. Therefore, I request that this be shown. It's a minute. It's less than a minute, really. A minute, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Williamson, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was one other housekeeping matter that Mr. Bos pointed out to me after Mr. Dokmanovic finished testifying. And that was the translation of the statement that was given in the prison, in Serbo-Croatian that was referred to by Mr. Dokmanovic. I failed to tender that into evidence. So at this time I would seek to tender that as Prosecutor's Exhibit 128B. Is that correct, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we have come to the end of our hearing. Tomorrow, we will, first of all, introduce evidence -- thank you. We will finish with -- probably you will come with a jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Believe it or not, I have finished. Tomorrow afternoon, I am going to bring you the jacket, but I only reserve the right for certain written documents that I received and that are not related to Dokmanovic but the international conflict, et cetera, that I take a look (sic) at that. So perhaps I will give that to you tomorrow. But I kindly ask you now -- you know, it's become a rule already that I'm surprised by the Prosecution every day, they surprise me with something every day. Can I find out today, now that I have finished everything, who am I going to hear tomorrow? Or am I supposed to be surprised again by that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Williamson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, just to respond to this about surprising him. During the course of cross-examination of our witnesses, Mr. Fila presented documents to all of these witnesses, he presented newspaper articles that he did not show to us beforehand. That's the nature of cross-examination. We did not object to that at any point. And we have followed the same practice during the course of cross-examining witnesses. It is a different matter when we are presenting evidence as part of our case in chief or as part of our rebuttal, and in that situation, we have tried to provide it to him in advance on all occasions. The witness that we would call tomorrow would be Mr. Curtis as our first rebuttal witness in reference to two issues: The issue of the testimony of Mr. Novakovic and the statement that was given by Mr. Dokmanovic to Mr. Curtis in Sombor. This was previously provided to Mr. Fila along with the tapes, and at that time we had indicated that we had no intention to lead this evidence. However, if Mr. Fila asked questions to Mr. Dokmanovic during the course of his examination-in-chief, we would then feel that it was open for us to cross-examine on those issues. So we would present Mr. Curtis on those two limited issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Only Mr. Curtis tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Might we ask that if Mr. Fila is bringing this jacket tomorrow afternoon, would it be possible to just have the session in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: As I understand it, Mr. Fila is going to be bringing this overcoat in the afternoon. We have been very involved in preparing for cross-examination, so if we might have the morning to prepare and then present this tomorrow afternoon? I think it will be relatively brief. I think that we can finish in an hour and a half perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the way it is. The aeroplane from Belgrade arrives somewhere around 2.00. Before 3.00, I cannot receive this. As far as the notes of Mr. Curtis are concerned, I did not mention during the examination whether Mr. Dokmanovic talked to Mr. Curtis and what he said, et cetera. Let me be quite clear. Everything that happened after the event of 1991 I used this only in terms of the proceedings because you, when determining the sentence, you have to see the extent to which the accused cooperated with the Tribunal, that is to say, with the Prosecutor, and that is what I asked him about, whether he talked to the authorities of the Tribunal. I did not ask him about the contents of these discussions. I did not ask about that, and I'm not interested in that. And that is why I oppose the questioning of Mr. Curtis in that direction. And I cannot have this enter the transcript -- I mean that he talked to Mr. Curtis and others -- if I do not pose that question. And I did not ask what they talked about. Please take a look at the transcript. I never asked that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my recollection --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Williamson asked that, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my recollection is a little bit different, that some questions were posed to him about the substance of what was said. I don't want to get into an argument with Mr. Fila on this issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: -- But I believe that I am correct on this issue. Certainly the notes that I took during the course of his testimony indicated that some questions were asked about the substance of what was said when Mr. Dokmanovic spoke with Mr. Curtis. I never would have posed the question to him otherwise. But it's something that we can leave and review the transcript and go from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Didn't ask trait. Please take a look at that. It is only important for me before this Honourable Court to say that Mr. Dokmanovic talked and nothing else. I'm not interested in anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We will take a look at the transcripts and see what to do. In any case, tomorrow afternoon at 3.30 we have a Status Conference in a different case and -- I wonder whether we can bring it forward? We could hold the status conference at 3.00, from 3.00 to 4.00, and I wonder whether it is too late to start at 4.00 with this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, it's not. But, Your Honour, I don't think you have a status conference, I think you have a telephone over here -- Celebici is here tomorrow, I think. That is what I was told. Oh, sorry, sorry, sorry. There's the man who knows. Sorry, sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will be in Celebici and I'm sure it's going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, it's a status conference, and counsel is coming here. We would like to suggest that we should hold a hearing tomorrow at 11.00. Would that suit you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, 11.00 is fine. It would just help us to have a little bit of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And then we will continue in the afternoon after the status conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I agree to everything. But tomorrow I just need to see Mr. Curtis. I mean, not to see someone else who happened to be passing by and to come tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we adjourn now, and we will reconvene tomorrow at 11.00.
